title: Berthe Morisot's birth chart
metaDescription: Berthe Morisot's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.2° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled fall in cardinal signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. Cardinal weight is read as initiative: the instinct to be the reason something began.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 24.2° Capricorn — deep enough in the third decan (20°–30°) that Mercury, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (10.6°), Venus in Pisces (5.5°), Mars in Libra (21.7°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Mars hold the closest angle here — a square, 2.5° wide. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Neptune at 2.8°, and Mars opposition Pluto at 3.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Pluto while both square the Sun. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. Mercury makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. Venus in Pisces at 5.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Libra at 21.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 10.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 3 fire, 2 earth, 2 water, 2 air; by modality, 4 cardinal, 4 mutable, 1 fixed. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Nothing was retrograde that day, which is less common than it sounds.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
